findings.minimal_fix: Normalize physical_pci_id to canonical lowercase [domain:]bus:device.function hex format and strip whitespace/padding before duplicate checking and format verification.
findings.reason: _validate_four_gpu performs raw string membership check without normalizing PCI bus identifiers (e.g. casing, leading domain zeros, spacing), allowing alias representations of identical physical GPUs to bypass the distinct device check. Missing verification of known full physical PCI format.
findings.test: Pass device list containing duplicate physical GPUs formatted with different casing or domain prefixes (e.g. '0000:01:00.0' and '01:00.0'); validator accepts them as distinct instead of REFUSED.

findings.minimal_fix: Validate finite parity data with exact numerical bit error tolerances and hashes, rather than accepting bare boolean assertions. Require allocator exception/rejection evidence for 1-card and 3-card capacity refusals.
findings.reason: Validator accepts forged boolean flags (parity_check_passed: True, one_card_capacity_refusal: True, three_card_capacity_refusal: True, logits_reference_match: True) without verifying finite parity numerical metrics, exact tolerance hashes, or actual driver/allocator refusal payloads.
findings.test: Submit receipt with synthetic boolean flags set to True but lacking parity tolerance metrics, allocator error logs, and numerical tensor diffs; validator improperly proves claims.

findings.minimal_fix: Validate observed_timestamp against maximum staleness window relative to receipt execution time, and verify that memory_kind is DEDICATED on each individual device rather than a single top-level string.
findings.reason: observed_timestamp check only requires ts > 0, accepting arbitrary historical or stale timestamps (e.g. ts = 1000 from 1970). Memory kind is checked once at the top level rather than validating all 4 discrete cards as DEDICATED, and measured_peak_allocations items are not validated with is_valid_number.
findings.test: Submit observed_timestamp = 1000 and devices with shared memory; validator accepts stale timestamp and passes DEDICATED_CAPACITY claim without per-device inspection.

findings.minimal_fix: Enforce that total_unique_resident_bytes exceeds discrete 8GB single-card budget and reject arbitrary policy caps that do not reflect physical VRAM pooling.
findings.reason: Validator only rejects policy limits <= 32 MiB, permitting artificial policy limits like 64 MiB or 512 MiB to pass as qualification for dedicated multi-card capacity without proving true discrete 8GB physical VRAM pooling or actual model capacity.
findings.test: Submit artificial_policy_limit_mib = 64 with tiny resident bytes (1000 bytes); validator accepts receipt as qualifying multi-card pooling.

findings.minimal_fix: Assemble shapes in topological connectivity sequence or fuse all connected core components as a compound/union before asserting len(fused.Solids) == 1 on the completed core.
findings.reason: Incremental fusion loop immediately checks len(fused.Solids) == 1 after each fuse. shapes[0] is the bottom base plate (Z=0..4) and shapes[1] is the top plate (Z=206..210) separated by a 202 mm vertical gap. Fusing two disjoint shapes yields 2 solids, triggering RuntimeError('disconnected or invalid shape after fuse') on the very first iteration.
findings.test: Execute build(cfg, out_dir); shapes[0].fuse(shapes[1]) creates 2 disjoint solids and crashes at line 48.

findings.minimal_fix: Assign Label to the FreeCAD DocumentObject returned by doc.addObject('Part::Feature', ...), not to the underlying Part.TopoShape geometry.
findings.reason: Part.makeBox returns a Part.Shape / Part.TopoShape OCC BRep wrapper which does not possess a Label property in FreeCAD C++ bindings, causing AttributeError when setting b.Label or d_box.Label.
findings.test: Run Part.makeBox(10,10,10).Label = 'test' in FreeCAD Python; raises AttributeError.

findings.minimal_fix: Set printed core depth based on structural rails allowing card overhang within print limits, and compute core_bbox_mm from fused.BoundBox.XLength, YLength, ZLength.
findings.reason: core_D is set to full card length cL (199 mm), which exceeds print limit lD (188 mm) at rotation 0, causing line 25 to raise ValueError before build even starts. Card overhang is explicitly permitted by the specification. Additionally, core_bbox_mm in state.json is hardcoded to analytical values rather than actual OCC BRep BoundBox dimensions.
findings.test: Invoke build with default config at rot=0; raises ValueError: core bbox 170x199x210 exceeds print limit 200x188x254.

findings.minimal_fix: Explicitly reject bool with if isinstance(v, bool): raise ValueError(...).
findings.reason: In Python, isinstance(True, int) is True, so boolean values passed for dimension parameters (e.g. gap = True) bypass validation and are accepted as 1.0 mm, violating strict bool/nonfinite schema handling.
findings.test: Pass cfg['schema']['gap'] = True; build accepts True without raising ValueError.
